best_field_traits: Annual grass with often ascending or spreading branches, less filmy and flexuous than Japanese brome.
Lanceolate to oblong elongated spikelets often ~25–50 mm with 8–20 florets, much larger than typical Japanese brome.
Mature fertile lemma usually ~12–18 mm and awned around 6–12 mm in GrassBase treatment; measurements overlap.
Membranous ligule, hairy to nearly smooth sheaths, variable leaf-blade pubescence.
Awn arises from notched lemma tip; detailed shape/length and glume nerves require hand lens.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Full plant and base to document annual habit
Entire panicle including all branch junctions
Close one long many-flowered 25–50 mm spikelet against mm ruler
Close glumes and fertile lemma teeth/awn insertion
True ligule, lower sheath and hair bases
crew_field_check: LOOK AT THE SPIKELET, NOT JUST THE DROOP: all four bromes have several florets stacked along one spikelet, often with lemma awns. First decide ANNUAL vs PERENNIAL, then count florets, measure the entire spikelet, individual lemma and awn, and inspect the glume veins and leaf sheath hairs. Nodding inflorescences or long awns alone are not a species ID.
Measure actual mature spikelet(s) with a millimeter ruler.
Inspect lemma/glume or true ligule ONLY where detailed pixels or a collected macro are actually available.
Record uncertain grass to genus, don't force the species from one photo.

comparisons.key_distinctions: B. japonicus has often smaller ~10–15 mm spikelets and a delicate, sometimes kinked drooping panicle. Native B. texensis often has 9–12 mm lemmas and 6–10 mm awns, but forms overlap; determine on mature dissected spikelets. B. pubescens is perennial and has broad softer foliage, relatively short straight awns and an open drooping woodland panicle.

visual_comparison.memory_rule: Annual japonicus / lanceolatus / texensis versus perennial woodland pubescens. Small loose kinked heads japonicus; giant lance-shaped spikelets lanceolatus; damp shaded perennial pubescens; Texas annual texensis demands short-awn/lemma comparison.
